newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal may get car part imports licence.
newsitem.headline: Universal may get car part imports licence.

text.p: The Polish Universal trader may receive a licence for duty-free imports of parts for Hyundai car assembly from the new economy ministry after it was refused one by the old foreign trade ministry, a daily newspaper said.
Gazeta Wyborcza quoted Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek as saying he told the appropriate subordinate department head that Universal's request for such a permit was justified.
"In a letter to the appropriate department head I suggested that the request of Universal about the (duty-free) imports of parts for the assembly of Hyundai cars is justified," Kaczmarek said.
In August last year the government issued a regulation under which only already existing car assembly plants could import car parts duty-free.

Universal had applied for the permit saying it had a Hyundai assembly plant in the town of Plonsk but the then foreign trade ministry ruled that the facilities were not what it understood by a car assembly plant.

At the start of this year, already after the reform of Polish administration which scrapped the foreign trade ministry and established the economy ministry, Universal re-applied to the new ministry for the permit.
